body.text: In a single day, the federal executive branch gave up two long-held positions against gun owners.

DOJ's Office of Legal Counsel concluded the federal ban on handgun sales to 18-to-20-year-olds is unconstitutional, and the President ordered DOJ not to appeal the ruling gutting the NFA's registration scheme. Neither is a statute and neither is a Supreme Court decision — both are the government declining to defend its own law.

facts.title: 1. DOJ OLC: under-21 handgun-sale ban unconstitutional
2. No appeal ordered in Silencer Shop Fdn v. ATF (NFA)
3. NICS Monitoring — day 3, advocacy analysis only

body.text:
• OLC opinion: §§ 922(b)(1)/(c)(1) unenforceable vs dealers. Opinion, not law.
• NFA non-appeal confirmed by CBS + Congress. Relief is party-scoped, not nationwide.
• Maryland judge enjoins place-of-worship ban — one synagogue, one rabbi only.
• DOJ sues San Jose over ~$1,600 carry-permit fees. Nothing enjoined.

No item reached the volcanic tier for a 5th run: in both lead cases the government declined to defend a law rather than a court striking one down, and nothing a member may lawfully do changed today. Friday ballot sweep ran and returned nothing new. No peer move, day 18.
